title: Migration notice patterns and escalation matrix + Terraform hints for private deploys
content:
Purpose
This is a working draft: patterns and copy for customer communications during private deployments (VPC/on-prem) migrations and upgrades, plus a compact Terraform/operators appendix and an escalation matrix. Aim: provide a repeatable, low-friction path for upgrades with clear comms, predictable rollback hooks, and minimal customer ops load.

Audience
- Solutions/SEs preparing customer notices
- Eng private-deploy teams executing upgrades
- Customer success/ops for escalation and post-mortems

High-level approach (pattern)
1) Discovery & safe window negotiation: collect maintenance windows, blackout dates, and critical business times from the customer (use form: link to intake).
2) Dry-run in a staging mirror (customer or Redwood-hosted mirror) and surface diffs: drift in TF state, provider updates, image hashes.
3) Announce 72h, 24h, 4h, and 15m notices with progressively specific technical detail.
4) Run upgrade with monitoring + canary checks. If canary fails, automatic rollback to pinned version and immediate notification.
5) Post-upgrade audit and short follow-up note + SLO measurement for the next 72h.

SLO/SLA summary (for comms)
- Baseline SLO targets (example language for customer-facing copy):
  - Service availability: 99.95% monthly for API endpoint responding to signed requests.
  - Tail latency: 99th percentile response time < 500ms for short text generation (< 128 tokens) under dedicated capacity.
  - Inference correctness QA: no regression in customer-provided prompt set > 2% mismatch rate vs baseline (for model swaps).
- SLA credit-trigger example (internal note): any sustained degradation > 30 minutes below availability SLO during a Redwood-initiated upgrade qualifies for pro-rated service credit. Full terms referenced in the contract.

Pre-upgrade checklist (operator quicklist)
- Confirm customer maintenance approval and alternate fallback window.
- Tag and lock the TF workspace: remote state with write-lock enabled.
- Snapshot remote state and S3/GCS bucket of model artifacts.
- Export running KV caches (where applicable) or mark caches ephemeral for easy rebuild.
- Record current model hash / docker image digest / TF module version.
- Confirm runbooks & rollback sequence (see below).

Rollback plan (must be rehearsed)
- Immediate criteria for rollback: failed canary health checks, API errors > 5% of requests in 10 minutes, or customer request.
- Rollback actions: reapply pinned TF state, redeploy previous model image digest, flush ephemeral caches or re-route traffic to standby region.
- Post-rollback: open incident, trigger root-cause, provide timeline to customer within 6 hours.

Escalation matrix (short form)
- Level 1 (on-call eng-private-deployments): first touch. Slack: #private-deploy-oncall, phone: +1-XXX-OPL-ONC (placeholder).
- Level 2 (release-engineering lead): escalate if unresolved after 15 minutes or risks customer SLA.
- Level 3 (SRE + Eng manager): escalate for persistent degraded latency or data integrity concerns.
- Customer success engagement: notify at first escalation; loop in customer PM for decisions about extended maintenance.

Customer comms cadence & sample templates
(Variables used: {{CUSTOMER_NAME}}, {{MAINT_WINDOW}}, {{TIMEZONE}}, {{IMPACT_SCOPE}}, {{ROLLBACK_PLAN_URL}}, {{CONTACT_ESCALATION}})

Initial planning (email) — 72 hours out\Subject: Planned maintenance: Redwood private deployment upgrade for {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} — {{MAINT_WINDOW}}\\nHi {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} team,\\nWe are planning a routine upgrade of the Redwood private control plane and inference runtime on {{MAINT_WINDOW}} ({{TIMEZONE}}). Expected impact: brief rolling restarts of inference nodes, small blips for in-flight requests; we expect no customer data loss.\\nAction requested: please confirm the maintenance window or propose an alternate by replying to this thread. Full runbook and rollback plan: {{ROLLBACK_PLAN_URL}}.\\nThanks,\\nRedwood Private Deploys Ops

24-hour reminder (short)\Subject: Reminder — Redwood maintenance for {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} in 24 hours
Hi — just a reminder that the upgrade is scheduled in 24 hours. We will post a 4-hour and 15-minute notice with more details.\\nIf you need to reschedule: contact {{CONTACT_ESCALATION}}.

4-hour technical notice (detailed)\Subject: 4-hr pre-notice: maintenance details & canary plan — {{CUSTOMER_NAME}}
- Start: {{MAINT_WINDOW}} (TZ: {{TIMEZONE}})
- Duration: 60–90 minutes typical (may vary by cluster size)
- Impact: rolling restarts; ephemeral cache invalidation; brief increased latencies during canary windows
- Canary plan: 2 nodes for 10 minutes; success criteria: 95th percentile < 500ms and error rate < 0.5%
- Rollback URL and playbook: {{ROLLBACK_PLAN_URL}}

15-minute (final) Slack + email\Slack (short): "FYI {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} maintenance starting in 15m — monitoring channel: <link>. Ops oncall: +1-XXX. Expected duration ~1h."
Email body: short copy explaining start and where to find live updates (status page link).

Post-upgrade summary (template)\Subject: Maintenance complete — Redwood upgrade for {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} — {{MAINT_WINDOW}}
Summary: upgrade completed at {{COMPLETE_TIME}}. Canary metrics: pass/fail with short numbers. User-visible impact: none / brief errors (X requests affected). Next steps: monitoring window (72h) and follow-up check-in scheduled.

Operator runbook snippet (commands & TF hints)\- Lock state: terraform state pull > state-YYYYMMDD.tfstate; enable remote state locking in backend.
- Dry-run: terraform plan -var-file=customer.tfvars -out=plan.out; review provider/plugin version deltas.
- Apply with limited concurrency: terraform apply -target=module.node_pool[0] plan.out (use targeted applies only for known safe modules).
- Canary roll: use workspace/labels to set 10% traffic to canary via routing rules (examples below).

Compact Terraform appendix (notes for module maintainers / SE)\- Module versioning: always publish a semver tag and a changelog link; prefer patch releases for non-breaking fixes.
- State migration: add a migration step in the module README including 'terraform state mv' commands where resource names change.
- Remote state: require customers to use a remote state backend with locking (S3+DynamoDB, GCS with object locking). Document minimal IAM permissions.
- Provider upgrades: avoid major provider bumps inside the same maintenance unless necessary. When required, provide a one-off migration script and dry-run logs.
- Example snippet (recommended variables to expose to customers):
  - node_pool_count (number)
  - canary_percentage (number)
  - model_artifact_digest (string) — pinned by default
  - rollout_strategy (string) — {blue-green, rolling, canary}

Example Terraform operational commands (docs consumer copy)
- Snapshot state: aws s3 cp s3://tf-state/{{workspace}}/state.tfstate ./state-backup-{{date}}.tfstate
- Import existing resource: terraform import module.model.aws_ecr_image.model[0] <ecr-image-id>
- Force taint & re-create: terraform taint module.node_pool[0].instance && terraform apply -auto-approve

Routing & canary patterns (ops)
- Canary via edge router: tag 10% of requests by header or token; monitor metrics for 15 minutes; promote if stable.
- Blue/green alternative: maintain standby model fleet; flip traffic at LB level; keep old fleet alive for quick rollback.

Post-upgrade monitoring window & SLA follow-up\- Monitor abs metrics for 72 hours: availability, 95th/99th latency, error rates on inference.
- If any SLO drift > 0.5% persists for more than 60 minutes, notify customer and open a follow-up remediation plan.

Customer-facing status page blurb (short)\We performed a routine upgrade to the Redwood inference runtime for {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} on {{MAINT_WINDOW}}. The upgrade completed successfully. No persistent customer impact observed. If you notice any issues, please contact {{CONTACT_ESCALATION}}.

Open questions / decision items (for this draft)\- Do we require explicit signed acceptance for upgrades that may affect latency > 5% for short windows?
- Should we provide a paid expedited rollback service?
- Standardize phone escalation list vs. email-only for customers that do not accept phone contact.

Notes & references\- See PD-412 for the ticketed upgrade plan and dry-run artifacts.
- Terraform module PR #98 contains the proposed canary variables and state migration helpers.
